preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following clinical scenario to answer the next TWO questions.

Andrew is a 65-year-old man who presents to your walk-in clinic with dyspnea on exertion,

fatigue, and angina. He has a 40 pack-year smoking history and regularly consumes alcohol.

When auscultating his heartbeat, you notice a systolic murmur loudest at the base, and the

presence of S4. Based on this presentation, you suspect aortic stenosis.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following passage to answer the next THREE questions.

A 50-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with chest tightness, shortness of

breath, and with bradycardia, with a past medical history remarkable for coronary artery disease.

The physician orders an immediate ECG which is strongly suggestive of an inferior myocardial

infarct, with leads indicating ST depression and T wave inversion.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following passage to answer the next TWO questions.

A 70-year-old patient presents to your clinic with leg pain in both calves. The patient explains

the pain has been persistent over the past 6 months but it’s only noticeable when he does

laborious tasks such as mowing the lawn or shoveling the snow. Other than a few instances the

patient does not describe this as a large hindrance in his life. The patient lives a sedentary life, he

is a chronic smoker, and a recent lipid panel indicated hyperlipidemia.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following question stem to answer the next TWO questions.

Abigail is a 55-year-old nurse who works in the emergency department. One day while working,

she started feeling palpitations and checked herself in to be seen by a physician. Upon triage, her

heart rate was 130 bpm and her BP was measured at 150/95 mmHg. Her past medical history

includes hypertension but is otherwise unremarkable.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following prompt to answer the following TWO questions.

Taylor is an 80-year-old patient with recently diagnosed atrial fibrillation secondary to mitral

stenosis. The physicians and Taylor have chosen not to return her heart to normal sinus rhythm,

but instead to reduce her ventricular rate and reduce the risk of stroke associated with atrial

fibrillation.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A patient presents to the ER with SOB at rest, orthopena, confusion and dizziness. On examination you hear crackles in the lungs, and find a narrow pulse pressure. A chest x ray reveals pulmonary edema.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 72-year-old male patient, originally from Eastern Europe, presents with atrial fibrillation of unknown duration. On history, you note that he had an MI ten years prior. He also has long-standing rheumatic heart disease and mitral stenosis. He has no history of stroke or TIA, diabetes, or pulmonary disease. He has long-standing fibromyalgia. He drinks approx. 10 drinks a week and does not smoke. His current medications include a statin for hyperlipidemia, an ACE Inhibitor for hypertension, and gabapentin for fibromyalgia.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following stem to answer the next TWO Questions.

You are a third-year clerk interviewing a patient during your family medicine rotation. Mr.

Wiggum, a 53-year-old police officer, is concerned about some difficulty swallowing. He reports

that both foods and liquids feel like they get stuck in his chest, and that this has been fairly

constant over the past 4 years. Upon questioning, he admits that he rarely experiences associated

heartburn or chest pain, and that his symptoms are worse at night.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A pregnant patient receives some bloodwork indicating elevated levels of fractionated ALP. Based on her presentation of symptoms, the physician is concerned about the possibility of bile duct obstruction.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following clinical scenario to answer the next TWO questions.

A 35 year old woman presents with post-prandial epigastric pain. She has been taking Aspirin for

chronic headache. You are suspicious of a peptic ulcer.

preamble.title: The case - Diane
preamble.html: The case. Diane comes into your clinic and describes recurrent abdominal pain at least once a week as well as an associated increase in bowel movements. She notes her stools have been very water as well. She has been experiencing this for the past year and is otherwise healthy.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A patient presents with abdominal cramping, fever and bloody stools that have been ongoing for 5 days. You take a detailed history and learn that they recently completed a course of antibiotics for a UTI. You have high clinical suspicion that the patient has a C.diff infection.

preamble.title: The case - Taylor
preamble.html: The case. Taylor is a 55-year-old female patient presenting to your clinic in a distressed tachypneic state. A physical exam reveals pitting edema to the level of the kneecap.

preamble.title: The case - Mr. Taylor
preamble.html: The case. Mr. Taylor presents to the ER in a distressed and fatigue state. After the patient's vitals are taken and maintained, an arterial blood gas is taken which reveals the patient has metabolic acidosis. ABG values are displayed below. pH: 7.25 HCO3-: 12 Anion gap: 20

You are a first-year resident in emergency medicine and your attending physician is quizzing you

on the diagnosis of one of her patients. The 24-year-old patient’s mother found her unconscious

and subsequently called EMS. Since the patient was unconscious, no patient history could be

obtained. A portion of the patient’s bloodwork is shown below.

Blood pH: 7.24

pCO2: 29 mmHg

HCO3-: 14 mmol/L

serum Na+: 136 mmol/L

serum Cl-: 110

albumin: 40 g/L

urine pH: 6.3

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following question stem to answer the next TWO questions.

A patient presents to the emergency room concerned about pain in his left flank that developed

over the past 2 days. Ultrasound reveals a mass obstructing the patient’s left ureter and

hydronephrosis of the left kidney. The patient’s right ureter and kidney are normal. Urinalysis

reveals a normal creatinine and BUN levels, and no evidence of a UTI. Assume the mass is

benign.

preamble.title: The case - Taylor
preamble.html: The case. As a physician you’re currently seeing a patient, Taylor (a 35-year-old female) with severe renal colic and an inability to void for the past 12+ hours. Their BUN/creatinine ratio is significantly elevated, and a renal ultrasound reveals bilateral obstruction of the proximal ureters.

preamble.title: The case - Brian
preamble.html: The case. Brian is a 22 year old international student from Taiwan. He presents with a 2 day history of edema, nausea & fatigue. Urinalysis finds 2.3 g of protein in his urine over 24 hours as well as red blood casts.

preamble.title: The case - Judy
preamble.html: The case. 55 year old Judy was recently diagnosed with urgency incontinence.

preamble.title: The case - Tyler
preamble.html: The case. Tyler is an 18-year-old male, who was incidentally found to have 2 mm ureteric stone. He is asymptomatic.

preamble.title: The case - Francis

A 24-year-old patient arrives at the ER with signs of hypoxemia. Their arterial blood gas

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following prompt to answer the next TWO questions.

A 25-year-old patient presents to your clinic with a mild fever, malaise and shortness of breath.

After taking a history (which revealed an extensive hospital stay this past week after breaking his

femur playing football) and an unremarkable physical exam, the physician suspects pneumonia.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following stem to answer the next THREE questions.

A 40-year-old man presents to the ER coughing up blood with complaints of dyspnea and chest

pain. The patient’s previous history shows a history of epistaxis, skin lesions, and hematuria

(blood in urine). A prior V/Q scan at the hospital also shows several lung compartments as

physiologic dead spaces. A chest X ray conducted at the ER visit shows diffuse alveolar markings

across both lungs.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following clinical scenario to answer the next TWO questions.

A 58-year-old woman presents with a large lung nodule and significant risk factors for cancer.

Upon investigations, the lung nodule was found to be 4cm, and ipsilateral subcarinal lymph node

involvement was observed. Further, a malignant pleural effusion was also present. PET/CT

showed no further organ involvement.
